steps.stdout:
ste_check.mjs: ASD-STE100 (Issue 9) checker for docs/ prose and source doc comments.

Usage:
  ste_check.mjs <path>...            check markdown files, directories, or source files
  ste_check.mjs --glossary-report docs/   org and project glossary terms, conflicts between the two levels, unused project terms
  ste_check.mjs --status             show which STE word source is in use (pack, word list, or built-in only)
  ste_check.mjs --lookup WORD...     show the dictionary entry for a word (needs the agent pack)

Word source, resolved in this order:
  1. The ASD-STE100 agent pack at $STE_AGENT_PACK, or at <skill>/references/asd-ste100-agent-pack/.
     Full rule 1.1: unapproved words fail with the dictionary's alternatives, unknown words warn
     as technical-noun candidates (1.5, 1.12), technical-category examples are permitted.
  2. STE_DICTIONARY=/path/words.txt, one approved word per line. Any word not in it fails 1.1.
  3. Neither: the built-in non-STE list only. The summary says "(1.1 partial)".

Exit 0: no mechanical failure. Exit 1: at least one mechanical failure. Exit 2: usage.

Mechanical [M]: 4.2 contractions, 5.1/6.1 sentence length, 6.6 paragraph length, 8.1 semicolon,
GR-6 Latin abbreviations, 1.1 non-STE words (built-in list, dictionary when present), 1.11 glossary synonyms,
1.8 a contradiction between the org glossary (<skill>/references/org-glossary.json) and the project glossary.
Heuristic [H]: 3.6 passive, 3.5 -ing, 3.4 complex tenses, 9.3 phrasal verbs, 2.1 noun clusters,
5.2 two instructions, 5.3 non-imperative step, GR-4 bare This, and with the pack: 1.5 unknown words,
1.7 a word the dictionary permits only as a technical noun or verb.
Waiver: an HTML comment `<!-- ste-ok: <rule|all> reason -->` on the line before the sentence's line.
